abstract.text: Re-skin the engine’s stock lines, and roll dice that replay.

inlineContent.text: Every line the engine can say on its own initiative lives on one value,

Rule bodies can vary their behavior with three helpers:

code: "The thief eyes you with polite menace.",
"The thief pretends not to notice you.",

inlineContent.text: All three draw from one stream whose position lives in the world state. That buys two guarantees:
Replays
: a world built with
plays out identically for the same seed and commands, on every platform — the backbone of transcript tests and reproducible bug reports. The plain
seeds fresh each run.
Saves
: the stream’s position is part of the saved state, so a restored game continues with exactly the randomness it would have had.
Pin the seed in a test the same way the engine’s own suite does:

code: let world = try GameWorld(game: MyGame(), seed: 42)

abstract.text: A uniform draw from the range, for rule bodies:
A line that is assembled when it prints rather than when it is written.
A subject a line is allowed to leave unsaid.
The subject of a line that has none.
A verb the parser understood, and the part of the sentence it still
wants.
Looking around a dark room. The line most likely to want
: it prints on every dark turn, in every dark room, and
a game whose darkness has anything in it — a companion, a sound, a smell
— has to check that the thing is still there before saying so.
A word outside the game’s whole vocabulary.
A place, and the thing the player is riding through it.
The name with its indefinite article, for listings (“a velvet cloak”,
“an apple”, “some rails”), or the name alone when it is a proper name
(“Mrs. Vane”).

Builds the world with a fixed random seed: the same seed and the same
commands replay the same game, on any platform — for transcripts,
tests, and bug reports.
One stock line, in whichever shape the game wants it: a fixed sentence,

about.
A phrase with its first letter capitalized, for a line that opens on

A fragment of what the player typed, quoted back at them.
The game’s own name, and the line under it.
